texts.01d2f0fa461d: The British Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (BCCSS) was established to epidemiologically follow up the entire population of survivors of childhood cancer to determine the risks of adverse health outcomes which might be increased as a consequence of treatment for childhood cancer. The resultant information is used to : inform and cousel survivors concerning their risks; provide an evidence base to rationally plan the clinical follow-up of survivors taking account of the risks experienced by groups of survivors who recieved specific types of treatment; plan new treatment protocols which maintain levels of cure, but minimise the risks of adverse health outcomes.
texts.5fa4e497d5a9: The objectives are to establish a national population-based cohort of 34000 individuals diagnosed with cancer before aged 15, between 1940 and 2005 inclusive, in Britain, and surviving at least 5 years from diagnosis. Investigate observed and expected risks of specific causes of death, subsequent primary cancers and other serious non-cancer morbidity using existing registries and databases including the national death and cancer registries, Hospital Episode Statistics for England, the Patient Episode Database for Wales, the Information Services Division linked database for Scotland and the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project for England and Wales.
